title: From a Hierarchy of Stochastic Differential Equations to a Hierarchy of Generalized Beta Distributions
abstract: We introduce a mean-reverting stochastic differential equation with a three-component stochastic term and show that it generates a hierarchy of steady-state (stationary) distributions. At the top level, the hierarchy is described by a modified-Beta distribution, while one- and two-parameter reductions produce compact-support, power-law-tailed, and exponential-type limiting families within a single stochastic framework.   We then construct two generalized extensions of this hierarchy. In the first, the power transformation is applied directly at the level of the stochastic differential equation; in the second, the same transformation is applied only after the stationary modified-Beta hierarchy has been obtained. While these two procedures agree on important lower branches and limiting cases they generally differ at the top level. The generalized hierarchy is therefore not unique: nonlinear transformation and stationary-state reduction do not commute.   For both routes, we derive the probability density and cumulative distribution functions, express their parameters in terms of the underlying stochastic dynamics, clarify the relations among their limiting cases, and compare the resulting families with the traditional Generalized Beta framework.
summary: This paper develops a comprehensive framework to characterize a hierarchy of probability distributions arising from a specific mean-reverting Stochastic Differential Equation. It introduces two methods—transforming the SDE versus transforming the stationary solutions—and proves that these two approaches yield different generalized distributions, highlighting a fundamental non-commutativity in the mathematical procedure.
main_problem: The paper investigates the stationary distributions generated by a mean-reverting Stochastic Differential Equation (SDE) and explores how these distributions can be generalized.
main_result: The authors show that generalizing the hierarchy via power transformations yields two distinct, non-commuting routes (dynamical vs. distributional), meaning the generalized hierarchy is not unique.
method: The methodology involves deriving stationary probability density functions (PDFs) from a master SDE and comparing results obtained by transforming the SDE versus transforming the resulting stationary PDFs.
model_or_system: The model is a mean-reverting SDE for a positively defined variable, which generates a hierarchy of distributions related to the Generalized Beta family. The analysis involves parameter reductions ($\kappa=0, \kappa_1=0, \kappa_2=0$) to map to known distributions.
key_observables: Probability density functions (PDFs) and cumulative distribution functions (CDFs) for the modified-Beta (mB) and generalized mGB families.
important_parameters: Mean-reversion rate ($\gamma$), mean-reversion scale ($	heta$), and stochastic coefficients ($\kappa, \kappa_1, \kappa_2$).
main_assumptions: The primary limitation noted is the non-commutativity of nonlinear transformation and stationary-state reduction, implying the generalized hierarchy is route-dependent.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the flow of the hierarchy in the Beta sector and the generalized sector via the two distinct transformation routes, while tables provide the explicit mathematical forms (PDFs/CDFs) for both generalized families.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the base hierarchy from the master SDE, then details two procedures for generalization (dynamical vs. distributional), and finally provides extensive mathematical tables comparing the resulting functional forms and parameters for both generalized families.
why_interesting: While the focus is on classical stochastic processes, the mathematical machinery of deriving complex, multi-parameter distributions from underlying dynamics (SDEs) is highly relevant to modeling non-equilibrium steady states in quantum systems.
